subject: Emotions
title: Affect Labeling
description: A fast breakdown of Affect Labeling for builders.

hook.text: You feel terrible. You say out loud: 'I feel anxious about tomorrow.' Instantly, the feeling loosens its grip.

buildup.text: Matthew Lieberman's fMRI studies show that putting feelings into words reduces amygdala activation.

discovery.text: Naming an emotion activates the prefrontal cortex, which dampens the emotional response. Words become medicine.

twist.text: Third-person self-talk works even better. 'Ethan is nervous' calms Ethan more than 'I am nervous.'

climax.text: Journaling works similarly: writing about emotions for 15 minutes reduces their intensity for days.

punchline.text: Name it to tame it. Language is the brain's off switch for panic.

quiz.question: What does affect labeling reduce in brain scans?
